question.text: Kalinga Capital (Cat II AIF) adds a new LP, Mr. Rohan Gupta, who commits INR 85 lakh. Mr. Gupta is NOT an Accredited Investor. Has the AIF complied with the minimum investment norm under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: Yes, because INR 85 lakh exceeds the INR 25 lakh minimum.
Yes, because the 75% investor-value threshold was met.
Yes, because the fund size is a private matter between GP and LPs.
No — the minimum investment from every non-Accredited investor must be at least INR 1 crore.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Chapter 12 (CTR Table 12.1) and Regulation 10: 'Minimum investment amount from every investor should be INR 1 crore' (except for Accredited Investors per the Third Amendment 2021). Mr. Gupta's INR 85 lakh commitment from a non-Accredited investor is a compliance breach. **The Trap:** INR 25 lakh is the minimum for Angel Funds (a Cat I sub-category) — not general Cat I/II. 75% by value is the winding-up threshold, unrelated. Privacy is not a compliance defence. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C, XIX-A both drill the INR 1 crore minimum. XIX-B Cat III uses the same INR 1 crore. XXI-B PMS has INR 50 lakh minimum (different). **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Train your fund-raising team to auto-screen commitments below INR 1 crore. For commitments on the margin, confirm Accredited Investor status in writing (SEBI-recognised certification) BEFORE accepting.
